1) Outline (sections A–H in exact order): A. Executive Summary (max 3 slides) — 1) board targets & three-year financial headline; 2) strategic thesis and prioritized bets; 3) top risks & asks of the board. B. Market and Competitive Overview — 1) TAM/SAM by segment and growth trends; 2) competitor moves & positioning map; 3) pricing & contract benchmarks; 4) regulatory landscape impacts per segment. C. Customer Segments and Needs — 1) segment profiles (mid-market tech, enterprise FS, professional services); 2) prioritized use cases and buyer personas; 3) segmentation refinements/opportunity scoring; 4) NRR and churn drivers by cohort. D. Product and Platform Strategy — 1) roadmap of core platform vs. incremental AI-enabled features grounded in current capabilities; 2) product-market fit gaps and required R&D/resources; 3) privacy, data residency, and regulatory controls (FS focus); 4) integration & developer ecosystem plan. E. Go-to-Market and Partnerships — 1) motion by segment (direct, AE, SDR, CS-led); 2) partner/channel experiments (ISVs, MSPs, referral/implementation partners); 3) pricing, packaging, and sales playbooks; 4) marketing demand-gen and case-study strategy. F. Financial Projections and Scenario Analysis — 1) base / upside / downside scenarios (revenue, margin, NRR) aligned to board targets; 2) unit economics, CAC payback, and cohort LTV; 3) capital needs and hiring plan; 4) sensitivity tables (must use finance templates). G. Risks, Dependencies, and Mitigations — 1) strategic, execution, and market risks; 2) regulatory & data-privacy risk and mitigation controls; 3) dependency map (key partners, tech, hires) and contingency plans. H. Implementation Roadmap (8 quarters, major milestones) — 1) product milestones (MVP AI features, compliance controls); 2) GTM milestones (partner launches, segment-focused sprints); 3) hiring & org milestones; 4) key metrics and gating criteria per quarter.

2) High-priority analytical questions to answer before locking strategy (grouped): Market — 1) What is realistic revenue run-rate upside in each core segment given current win rates and pipeline conversion (3-yr view)? 2) Which competitors are likely to compress pricing or bundle features and how quickly? Product — 3) What percent of customers use data/flows that permit immediate deployment of AI features without significant re-architecture? 4) Which product gaps (by effort) most materially constrain NRR improvements? GTM & Partnerships — 5) What are current CAC, sales cycle, and payback by segment and channel, and where are the biggest inefficiencies? 6) Which partner types (ISV, SI, MSP, marketplace) can deliver >2x ROI on GTM spend within 12 months? Financial & Ops — 7) How sensitive are operating margins to 10–20% variation in customer acquisition, churn, and R&D ramp? 8) What hiring/phasing constraints or key single-point-of-failure roles exist that would delay milestones? Risks/Compliance — 9) For enterprise FS customers, what are exact data-residency, audit, and vendor risk requirements that could add delivery cost or timeline?

3) Fragility hypotheses / areas to investigate (posed as questions): - Are our CAGR and 18%+ operating margin targets simultaneously achievable without either (a) materially compressing sales investment or (b) achieving faster-than-historical NRR improvement? - Is our assumed speed-to-market for AI-enabled features optimistic given current engineering backlog, data quality, and model ops readiness? - Could enterprise FS regulatory and procurement timelines (and required controls) extend sales cycles enough to undercut year‑2 revenue targets? - Do partner/channel experiments have realistic near-term capacity to scale, or are we underestimating partner onboarding and enablement costs? - Is our NRR improvement plan dependent on a small set of top customers or upsell plays that, if they falter, would breach the board NRR target?

1) Executive narrative: Base is the finance-built status‑quo plan that meets the board’s minimums through steady segment growth, margin discipline, and modest NRR improvement; Stretch layers prioritized AI modules (Compliance Co‑Pilot Lite + Auto‑Assist), accelerated partner co‑sell and GTM investment to pursue higher revenue and NRR while accepting higher near‑term spend and regulatory/operational execution risk.  
Both scenarios keep our three core segments and the 18% margin guardrail; the trade‑off is clear—Base minimizes upfront risk and preserves margin, Stretch frontloads investment to chase top‑end growth but requires faster model readiness, compliance validation, and partner ramp to avoid dilution of returns.

2) Key bets (distinguishing Stretch from Base): Pilot‑to‑scale Compliance Co‑Pilot Lite in FS (pilot Y1, scale Y2) — worth it because it defends/expands FS share despite compliance complexity; Expand Auto‑Assist for CS‑led expansion in mid‑market — worth it because modest automation can materially lift NRR and CS productivity; ISV/Integrator co‑sell pilots to accelerate reach — worth it because partners can multiply coverage faster than headcount alone; Packaged automation templates with PS co‑delivery — worth it because they shorten time‑to‑value and create repeatable upsell hooks.

3) Risks and asks for leadership: Confirm willingness to fund higher near‑term spend and hiring in Stretch; Align on appetite to lean harder into enterprise FS vs. mid‑market when trade‑offs arise; Confirm tolerance for accelerated compliance investments and agree pilot acceptance criteria for FS; Ask finance to validate the Stretch assumption of ~4–6pt NRR uplift from combined AI+CS and run sensitivity to +15–25% cloud/model‑ops and partner enablement costs; Validate telemetry/model‑training readiness with Product/CS before committing to pilot scale.
